name: Hover Micro-interaction (Subtle)
best_for: hover, button, opacity, lift, press feedback
framework_notes: Bind on mouseenter/mouseleave; in React wrap in a ref + useEffect (or onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave props directly calling gsap.to) Snippet: gsap.to(el, { y: -1, opacity: 0.9, duration: 0.15, ease: 'power1.out' });
keywords: hover, button, opacity, lift, press feedback
do: Keep displacement under 2px so it reads as feedback not motion
dont: Don't animate layout-affecting props (width/height/margin) on hover
performance_notes: Runs on transform/opacity only so it stays on the compositor thread

name: Hover Micro-interaction (Standard)
best_for: hover, card, scale, tilt, cursor feedback
framework_notes: Use gsap.quickTo(el, 'y') for cards with many hover targets to avoid re-creating tweens every event Snippet: gsap.to(el, { y: -4, scale: 1.02, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)', duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out' });
keywords: hover, card, scale, tilt, cursor feedback
gsap_snippet: gsap.to(el, { y: -4, scale: 1.02, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)', duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out' });
do: Pair with a matching mouseleave tween that reverses the same properties
dont: Don't leave the hover state stuck if the pointer leaves fast; always attach the reverse tween
performance_notes: quickTo() avoids GC churn on lists with 20+ hoverable cards

name: Hover Micro-interaction (Complex)
description: Trigger: hover + mousemove | Duration: 300-500ms | Easing: elastic.out(1,0.4)
framework_notes: Debounce is not needed since quickTo interpolates; remove listeners on component unmount in React/Vue to avoid leaks Snippet: const xTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'x', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'elastic.out(1,0.4)' }); const yTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'y', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'elastic.out(1,0.4)' }); el.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); xTo((e.clientX - r.left - r.width/2) * 0.3); yTo((e.clientY - r.top - r.height/2) * 0.3); });
gsap_snippet: const xTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'x', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'elastic.out(1,0.4)' }); const yTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'y', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'elastic.out(1,0.4)' }); el.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); xTo((e.clientX - r.left - r.width/2) * 0.3); yTo((e.clientY - r.top - r.height/2) * 0.3); });
do: Clamp the pull strength (e.g. * 0.3) so the element never fully leaves its hit box
dont: Don't apply magnetic effect to more than 1-2 focal elements per screen; it becomes noisy
performance_notes: Use will-change: transform on the target element for smoother compositing

name: Scroll Reveal (Subtle)
description: Trigger: scroll (viewport enter) | Duration: 300-400ms | Easing: power1.out
best_for: scroll, fade in, reveal, on view
framework_notes: Requires the ScrollTrigger plugin registered once via gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) Snippet: gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power1.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 90%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse' } });
keywords: scroll, fade in, reveal, on view
gsap_snippet: gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power1.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 90%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse' } });
do: Keep the y offset small (8-16px) so it reads as a fade, not a slide
dont: Don't reveal below-the-fold content needed for SEO/crawlers as invisible-by-default without a no-JS fallback
performance_notes: toggleActions 'play none none reverse' avoids re-triggering on every scroll direction change

name: Scroll Reveal (Standard)
description: Trigger: scroll (viewport enter) | Duration: 400-600ms | Easing: power2.out
best_for: scroll, slide up, staggered section, reveal
framework_notes: In React use useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: containerRef }) from @gsap/react to auto-cleanup on unmount Snippet: gsap.from(el.children, { opacity: 0, y: 24, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%' } });
keywords: scroll, slide up, staggered section, reveal
gsap_snippet: gsap.from(el.children, { opacity: 0, y: 24, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%' } });
do: Scope the ScrollTrigger to the section container so it doesn't re-scan the whole page
dont: Don't stagger more than ~8 children; beyond that the last items feel laggy
performance_notes: Set scroller/markers: false in production; markers is dev-only

name: Scroll Reveal (Complex)
description: Trigger: scroll (continuous scrub) | Duration: tied to scroll position | Easing: none (scrub-driven)
framework_notes: Pinning needs the section to have deterministic height; recalc ScrollTrigger.refresh() after images/fonts load Snippet: gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, start: 'top top', end: '+=150%', scrub: 1, pin: true } }).from('.headline', { opacity: 0, y: 40 }).to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: -20 }, '<');
gsap_snippet: gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, start: 'top top', end: '+=150%', scrub: 1, pin: true } }).from('.headline', { opacity: 0, y: 40 }).to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: -20 }, '<');
do: Use scrub: true or a small number (0.5-1.5) instead of instant jumps so it feels tied to the scrollbar
dont: Don't pin more than 1-2 sections per page; excessive pinning fights native scroll feel and hurts mobile UX
performance_notes: Pinning forces layout reflow; test on mid-tier mobile devices, not just desktop

name: Stagger List (Subtle)
description: Trigger: load or scroll | Duration: 250-350ms | Easing: power1.out
framework_notes: Select items with a stable class/data-attribute (not array index) so re-renders in React don't break targeting Snippet: gsap.from('.list-item', { opacity: 0, y: 8, duration: 0.3, stagger: 0.03 });
do: Keep per-item stagger delay small (0.02-0.04s) for lists longer than 10 items
dont: Don't stagger by more than 0.1s per item on long lists; total reveal time becomes sluggish
performance_notes: For virtualized lists, only animate items currently mounted in the DOM

name: Stagger List (Standard)
description: Trigger: load or scroll | Duration: 300-450ms | Easing: back.out(1.4)
framework_notes: grid: 'auto' lets GSAP infer rows/columns from a CSS grid layout for a natural wave stagger Snippet: gsap.from('.grid-item', { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start', grid: 'auto' }, ease: 'back.out(1.4)' });
gsap_snippet: gsap.from('.grid-item', { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start', grid: 'auto' }, ease: 'back.out(1.4)' });
do: Combine with from: 'center' for a bento-grid layout to draw the eye inward first
dont: Don't use back.out on dense data tables; the overshoot reads as sloppy on informational UI
performance_notes: Group DOM writes; avoid interleaving layout reads (getBoundingClientRect) between staggered tweens

name: Stagger List (Complex)
description: Trigger: load or scroll | Duration: 400-700ms | Easing: expo.out
best_for: stagger, wave, text reveal, split text
framework_notes: SplitText is a GSAP Club/paid plugin; confirm license before shipping and provide a plain fade fallback if unavailable Snippet: const split = new SplitText(headline, { type: 'chars' }); gsap.from(split.chars, { opacity: 0, y: 20, rotateX: -40, duration: 0.6, stagger: 0.015, ease: 'expo.out' });
keywords: stagger, wave, text reveal, split text
gsap_snippet: const split = new SplitText(headline, { type: 'chars' }); gsap.from(split.chars, { opacity: 0, y: 20, rotateX: -40, duration: 0.6, stagger: 0.015, ease: 'expo.out' });
do: Revert SplitText on unmount/cleanup (split.revert()) to restore original text nodes for accessibility tools
dont: Don't split-animate long paragraphs; reserve for short headlines (under ~8 words)
performance_notes: Splitting text creates one element per character; keep it to headline-length copy only for DOM size

name: Page Transition (Subtle)
description: Trigger: route change | Duration: 200-300ms | Easing: power1.inOut
framework_notes: Pair with the router's transition hooks (Next.js App Router transitions, React Router's useNavigate, Vue Router's beforeEach/afterEach) Snippet: gsap.to(main, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2, onComplete: () => { navigate(); gsap.fromTo(main, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.2 }); } });
gsap_snippet: gsap.to(main, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2, onComplete: () => { navigate(); gsap.fromTo(main, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.2 }); } });
do: Preload the destination route's critical assets before the exit tween finishes
dont: Don't block navigation on animation; cap exit duration at ~250ms so the app never feels unresponsive
performance_notes: Exit animation should always resolve faster than entrance (asymmetric timing) so back/forward feels snappy

name: Page Transition (Standard)
description: Trigger: route change | Duration: 400-600ms | Easing: power2.inOut
framework_notes: Keep the overlay element mounted at the layout root (outside the page component) so it survives the route swap Snippet: const tl = gsap.timeline(); tl.to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut' }).call(navigate).to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: -100, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut', delay: 0.1 });
gsap_snippet: const tl = gsap.timeline(); tl.to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut' }).call(navigate).to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: -100, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut', delay: 0.1 });
do: Show a lightweight loading indicator if the destination route's data fetch outlasts the overlay
dont: Don't tie the overlay's reveal directly to data-fetch completion without a max-wait timeout; a slow API stalls the whole transition
performance_notes: Prefer CSS transform (yPercent) over top/left to keep the overlay animation on the compositor thread

name: Page Transition (Complex)
description: Trigger: route change | Duration: 500-800ms | Easing: expo.inOut
framework_notes: Requires the GSAP Flip plugin; the 'from' and 'to' route must render the same element with a shared data-flip-id Snippet: const state = Flip.getState('.hero-image'); navigate(); Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'expo.inOut', absolute: true, zIndex: 100 });
gsap_snippet: const state = Flip.getState('.hero-image'); navigate(); Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'expo.inOut', absolute: true, zIndex: 100 });
do: Verify the shared element exists in both DOM states before calling Flip.from to avoid a silent no-op
dont: Don't use shared-element transitions across more than one element pair per navigation; compounding Flips are hard to time correctly
performance_notes: Flip recalculates layout (FLIP technique) so test on low-end devices for jank

name: Parallax Scroll (Subtle)
description: Trigger: scroll (continuous) | Duration: tied to scroll position | Easing: linear (scrub)
framework_notes: Apply parallax to background/decorative layers only, never to text or interactive controls Snippet: gsap.to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: 10, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, scrub: true } });
gsap_snippet: gsap.to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: 10, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, scrub: true } });
do: Keep the yPercent delta small (5-15) so foreground and background never desync distractingly
dont: Don't parallax body copy; it hurts reading comfort and can trigger motion sickness
performance_notes: will-change: transform on the parallax layer only; remove it after scroll settles to free GPU memory

name: Parallax Scroll (Standard)
description: Trigger: scroll (continuous) | Duration: tied to scroll position | Easing: linear (scrub)
framework_notes: Layer count beyond 3-4 has diminishing visual return and multiplies scroll-listener cost Snippet: gsap.utils.toArray('.parallax-layer').forEach((layer, i) => { gsap.to(layer, { yPercent: (i + 1) * -8, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: layer.parentElement, scrub: 0.5 } }); });
gsap_snippet: gsap.utils.toArray('.parallax-layer').forEach((layer, i) => { gsap.to(layer, { yPercent: (i + 1) * -8, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: layer.parentElement, scrub: 0.5 } }); });
do: Vary speed per layer (background slowest, foreground fastest) to sell the depth illusion
dont: Don't let parallax layers overflow their container; clip with overflow: hidden on the wrapper
performance_notes: Batch all layers under one ScrollTrigger container where possible instead of one per layer

name: Loading / Skeleton (Subtle)
description: Trigger: on mount / async wait | Duration: 1200-1600ms loop | Easing: sine.inOut
framework_notes: Kill the loop tween (tween.kill()) as soon as real content mounts to avoid orphaned repeating animations Snippet: gsap.to('.skeleton', { backgroundPosition: '200% 0', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut', repeat: -1 });
do: Use a CSS gradient background-position sweep rather than opacity pulsing; reads as 'loading' more clearly
dont: Don't run more than one shimmer loop per skeleton group; sync them under one timeline so the wave reads as a single unit
performance_notes: repeat: -1 tweens are cheap but must be explicitly killed on unmount or they leak in SPA route changes

name: Loading / Skeleton (Standard)
description: Trigger: on mount / async wait | Duration: 800-1200ms loop | Easing: power1.inOut
framework_notes: Wrap the whole loop timeline in useGSAP with { revertOnUpdate: false } in React so it isn't rebuilt every render Snippet: gsap.timeline({ repeat: -1 }).to('.loader-dot', { y: -8, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.15, yoyo: true, repeat: 1 } });
gsap_snippet: gsap.timeline({ repeat: -1 }).to('.loader-dot', { y: -8, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.15, yoyo: true, repeat: 1 } });
do: Cap total loop duration under ~1.5s so long waits don't feel like the UI froze on a single beat
dont: Don't use elaborate loaders for sub-300ms waits; they flash and feel worse than no indicator
performance_notes: Pause the timeline (tl.pause()) when the loading tab/view is not visible to save CPU on background tabs
